shapes: Above the eta is a single fused mark. Its right half is a thin wave rising to a rounded terminal at top-right (the circumflex/tilde stroke). Its left half is much heavier than a plain tilde lobe: a solid rounded blob at top-left that hangs down below the dip of the wave and tapers to a short tail going down-left. That is the comma (psili) shape of this font, as seen on ἐς, ἠχήεντα and αὐτίκα on the same line (blob at top, tail curling down-left), merged into the left end of the circumflex. No reversed-comma (dasia) form opening the other way. No two dots (no diaeresis). Nothing under the eta: the descender is clean and there is no iota subscript stroke. The other letters are plain γ and lunate-style ε.
